title: routes.v1 — a domain's declaration of the routes the gateway serves for it, and each route's policy
description: Each domain writes one `routes.v1.json` beside its service; the gateway assembles its route table from the manifests of the domains a deployment runs (`gateway/routes_manifest.py`). A row carries its policy as well as its scopes, so every policy key lives here: a new one is a contract change (lane:contract), not a loader edit. A forwarded domain may also carry `verbs` rows: policy for one verb behind the forward, read by the domain's own service, not the edge. Rules that span rows or manifests (one owner per (method, path); a forwarded row under its domain's prefix) are stated on Manifest and checked by validate.mjs over every manifest in the repository.

domain.description: the domain whose service is behind these routes; `gateway` is the edge's own two routes

owner.description: the repository path of the owning domain or service

presence_env.description: the setting whose presence means this domain is deployed; absent, its rows are not in the table and its routes answer 404

verbs.description: policy for one verb behind a forward, which the catch-all cannot carry: each row names the verb by its public path. The edge does not register these rows; the domain's service reads them (agent-api's `control_plane/route_policy.py`)

allOf.description: stream applies to a forwarded domain's literal rows only
mcp_reentry on an unscoped row is the edge's own identity read (`/auth/me`) only: no other unscoped row reaches the authorizer that reads it
verbs map onto the domain's own routes through its forward
a forwarded domain's rows carry no upstream: the forward is the one mapping

Manifest.$comment: Also checked by validate.mjs, across rows and manifests: (method, path) is declared by one manifest only; with a forward, every path is the edge prefix followed by literal segments and whole `{name}` parameters (no name twice), or the prefix's `{path:path}` catch-all. A `verbs` row is a path strictly under the edge prefix, and no (method, path) is in `verbs` twice. A row's `upstream` names no `{name}` parameter twice and none the row's own path lacks.

Forward.description: a domain the edge forwards wholesale: `/<edge_prefix><tail>` is sent upstream as `/<upstream_prefix><tail>`

scopes.description: the key scopes that may call the row; an empty list DECLARES the row unscoped (never an omission)

delegation.description: true: the row admits a worker's own delegation token; every other row refuses it

mcp_reentry.description: true: the row admits a worker's delegation token only on the MCP's re-entry, i.e. one row per route an mcp.tools.v1 tool calls back

stream.description: true: the edge relays the row's response as server-sent events

upstream.description: the route template the edge forwards this row to on the domain's service, when it is not the row's own path; its `{name}` parameters are the row's. The domain's service reads it to know which rows reach each of its routes. A forwarded domain carries none: its forward is the one mapping

allOf.description: a delegation row is scoped (an unscoped row never reaches the authorizer), and carries no mcp_reentry (the row already admits the token)
only a literal row streams, never the catch-all
mcp_reentry names one route an MCP tool calls back, never a catch-all that would admit every path under its prefix

person.description: true: the verb needs a person in the loop, and the service refuses a worker dispatched without one before the route runs

Refused.description: a refusal vector: `manifest` must be refused, for the reason `why` names
